issues.description: New branch's predicate `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` is too broad and captures navigation/dismissal keys.
issues.detail: The guard fires for every non-Tab key including arrow keys, Escape, Backspace, and modifiers, then forwards the event to the editor. The contract should narrowly target Enter/Return as the accept keys being disabled, not 'anything that isn't Tab'. Restructure the dispatch around an explicit 'is this an accept key right now?' predicate.

issues.description: Cross-module event re-dispatch via `textedit.keyPressEvent(event)` leaks editor internals into the popup.
issues.detail: Hiding the popup and directly invoking the parent editor's keyPressEvent couples the completion widget to the editor's exact event semantics and skips any focus/proxy logic Qt would insert. Prefer `hide()` plus `event.ignore()` so Qt's normal propagation delivers the key through the standard pipeline.

issues.description: Enter accept path is not cleanly short-circuited; downstream logic may still fire.
issues.detail: The new block is bolted into an already-overloaded keyPressEvent that handles Enter/Return/Tab together. Because the branch is spliced ahead of the `item is None` guard rather than restructuring dispatch, the downstream Enter-accept path can still execute for some items. Compute accept-key status once at the top and skip the accept branch entirely when disabled.

issues.description: `get_conf` called on every keypress for a static user preference.
issues.detail: A config dictionary walk runs in the hot path of typing inside the popup. Cache the value when the popup is shown or subscribe to config changes so toggling the setting still propagates. Not catastrophic, but unnecessary work on every keystroke.

issues.description: No test coverage for the new Enter-disabled branch.
issues.detail: Completion widget key handling regresses silently. Add a test that disables `use_enter_for_completions`, sends Enter, and asserts no completion is accepted (and that Tab still accepts). Prevents future maintainers from undoing this by accident.

issues.description: Missing written contract/docstring for the new option's behavior.
issues.detail: Neither the default, the conf page tip, nor the keyPressEvent branch states which keys accept, dismiss, or navigate when the flag is off. Also fix the awkward `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` to `key != Qt.Key_Tab` and document section ownership (`completions` vs `editor`) for the config key.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a small, useful patch (#12728) that lands with NEEDS-WORK. Core problems are taste and contract: the gate is spliced into an already-busy keyPressEvent as a special case, the predicate `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` is far too broad and captures navigation/dismissal keys, and the popup re-dispatches the event directly into the editor's keyPressEvent rather than using Qt-native propagation. Restructure dispatch around an explicit accept-key predicate, narrow the branch to Enter/Return, use `hide()` + `event.ignore()`, cache the config read, and add a test plus a written behavioral contract for the new option.
